narrative: OMX30 opens with tailwinds from continental Europe's overnight rally, particularly DAX strength at +0.77%. Technical setup remains constructively bullish: the index trades 6.3% above its 200-MA in a confirmed bull regime, MACD is above signal line with positive histogram at +2.882, and momentum (ROC-90) is strong at +6.6%, positioning us 0.8% from all-time highs. Commodity support—gold and copper both up over 1%—underpins mining and industrial cyclical exposure. However, weak ADX at 6.5 demands respect: trend strength is subdued despite direction, and elevated Stochastic K/D (73.4/69.5) flags early mean-reversion risk. US yields (5.162%, +0.94%) and VIX compression (-2.30%) provide conflicting signals; rates pressure growth/tech DCF but support banking NIM. Key watch: trade narrative escalation (tariffs, Brexit) could reignite volatility.
morningBrief: OMX30 enters Friday with moderately positive bias off DAX's overnight +0.77% lead and sustained technical strength above the 200-MA. MACD momentum remains positive, but weak ADX (6.5) cautions against over-confidence—bulls lack structural conviction. Opening levels: watch 3123 (pivot), with near-term resistance at 3180 (50-MA) and support at 3085 (lower Bollinger). Sector split: Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) benefit from stable USD/SEK and European momentum; Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) get a lift from elevated US yields (+94bp overnight) widening NIM. Boliden is a prime mover today on gold/copper strength—this is your best cyclical trade. Defensives (AstraZeneca, Essity) should outperform any risk-off into close. Trade tensions in headlines (Brexit tariffs, China auto duties) remain the wildcard; jobless claims at 14:30 CET could trigger volatility. Stay nimble on size given ADX weakness.
